biodiversity_overview.text: 30,582 GBIF occurrence records for 75 tracked species are attributed to Uttar Pradesh, spanning 1833-2026.
29,887 of these records (97.7%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 27, Magnoliopsida 15, Mammalia 12, Testudines 9, Squamata 5, Amphibia 3, Actinopterygii 3, Crocodylia 1.

threatened_species.text: 12 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
5 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Mugger Crocodile (VU), Tiger (EN), Asian Elephant (EN), Indian Rhinoceros (VU), Sloth Bear (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (4,063), Indian Grey-Hornbill (3,808), White-throated Munia (2,510), Indian Spot-billed Duck (2,269), Common Peafowl (2,230).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1,674 in 2016 to 344 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 1.98% of Uttar Pradesh's area (29 areas intersect the state).
24.2% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (7,238 of 29,887); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Eyed Turtle (0.55), Narrow-headed Softshell Turtle (0.54), Peacock Soft-shelled Turtle (0.50), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Uttar Pradesh (equal-weight reference): cell near 28.875N 77.625E (overall rank 9, median rank across weightings 16); cell near 26.625N 80.625E (overall rank 16, median rank across weightings 24); cell near 26.625N 82.125E (overall rank 67, median rank across weightings 84).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 4,097 km2 (1.7% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

51.0 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (1.24% of the 2000 extent; 0.12% in 2015-2024, rank 26 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2011 (7.23 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 2.11% of land and population density is 969.2 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
29% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
